## 1. KV (Key-Value) Caches: Foundations and Mechanics

### 1.1 The Transformer Attention Bottleneck
During autoregressive text generation, a Transformer decodes one token at a time. To compute the attention mechanism for token $t$, the model must attend to all previous tokens $\{x_1, \dots, x_t\}$. The standard attention computation is:

$$\text{Attention}(Q_t, K_{1:t}, V_{1:t}) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{Q_t K_{1:t}^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) V_{1:t}$$

Without optimization, computing $K_{1:t}$ and $V_{1:t}$ requires passing all prior tokens through the Transformer layers again. For a sequence of length $t$, this would scale quadratically as $\mathcal{O}(t)$ per layer per token generated, yielding $\mathcal{O}(t^2)$ total compute.

## 1. KV (Key-Value) Cache: Foundations and Mechanics

### 1.1 The Generative Bottleneck
Autoregressive models generate text token-by-token. To compute the logits for token $t$, the model requires the representations of all preceding tokens $\{x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{t-1}\}$. Running the full network from scratch for every generated token results in a computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ per sequence, rendering naive inference economically and practically unfeasible.
